152216.title: Landscape with a Hunter and other Figures
152216.creator: Jan Wijnants

editorial.note: Jan Wijnants (1631/32 - 1684). Landscape with a hunter and other figures, c. 1670. A half-dead tree dominates this work, a motif which the artist borrowed from Jacob van Ruisdael.
Aelbert Cuyp (1620 - 1691). Landscape with herdsmen and cattle, c. 1655. This landscape with its castle ruins evokes an idyllic atmosphere, reinforced by the contre jour effect.

An elegant party has gathered to set out on a hunt, a sport traditionally reserved for the nobility and wealthy leisured class in the 17th century. The man and woman on horseback in the foreground are therefore dressed in the latest fashion…
These shepherds seem to enjoy a simple and peaceful existence in a wide meadow. However, the life of farmers and shepherds was harder in reality.
A vast watery view dotted with numerous mills – at first sight this is a typical Dutch landscape. The purplish mountains on the horizon, however, sooner recall Italy.

152507.title: Landscape in the Dutch East Indies (Java?)

editorial.note: In 1858, the then 28-year-old Dutch painter Maurits van den Kerkhoff moved to Java, an island in Indonesia, which was a Dutch colony at the time. Van den Kerkhoff painted Javanese landscapes in a European manner.
